questions.enonce_markdown:
(a) What is computer ergonomics? (2 marks)

(b) Explain TWO ergonomics advice to design a school laboratory. Your answer should state what problem it will solve. (4 marks)

(c) Describe TWO health problems caused by prolong eye to monitor contact. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) Computer ergonomics (2 marks).** Ergonomics is the **study of how to design the equipment, the furniture and the working environment so that they fit the people who use them**. In computing, it means arranging the computers, the chairs, the desks, the lighting and the layout of the room so that the users work **comfortably, safely and efficiently**, and avoid health problems (fatigue, back pain, eye strain, RSI).

**(b) Two pieces of ergonomic advice for a school laboratory (4 marks)**

1. **Provide adjustable chairs with back support and desks of the right height, with the keyboard at elbow level and the screen at eye level, about an arm's length away.** *Problem solved:* it prevents **back, neck and shoulder pain** (bad posture) and **repetitive strain injury** of the wrists and hands, and keeps the students comfortable during long practical sessions.
2. **Provide proper lighting and screen positioning: use blinds or curtains, place the screens at right angles to the windows and away from direct light, use anti-glare screens and good, even room lighting.** *Problem solved:* it removes the **glare and reflections on the screen**, which cause **eye strain and headaches**.

(Other acceptable advice: good ventilation or air conditioning against heat and tiredness; enough space between the workstations and neat cables to avoid accidents; taking regular breaks.)

**(c) Two health problems of prolonged eye contact with the monitor (2 marks)**

- **Eye strain (computer vision syndrome):** dry, red, itching and tired eyes and blurred vision, because the user blinks less and the eyes focus on the screen for too long.
- **Headaches** (and tiredness), caused by glare, flicker and the continuous effort of the eyes. (Prolonged use may also disturb sleep because of the blue light of the screen.)

Prevention: regular breaks, for example looking away from the screen for 20 seconds every 20 minutes, and a correct screen brightness.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Define the following as used in data security.

(a) Data encryption. (2 marks)

(b) Data verification. (2 marks)

(c) Scamming. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) Data encryption (2 marks).** Encryption is the process of **converting data (plain text) into an unreadable form (cipher text) using an algorithm and a key**, so that only a person who has the correct key can decrypt and read it. It protects data that are stored (files, disks) or sent over a network (e-mail, online payment) in case they are intercepted or stolen.

**(b) Data verification (2 marks).** Verification is the process of **checking that the data entered into the computer are the same as the original (source) data**, i.e. that no mistake was made when copying them. It is done, for example, by **entering the data twice and comparing the two entries** (double entry) or by proofreading the screen against the source document. It does not prove that the data are reasonable (that is validation).

**(c) Scamming (2 marks).** Scamming is a **fraud in which a person is deceived, usually through the Internet, e-mail, text messages, social media or the telephone, in order to obtain money, goods or personal and banking information**. Examples: a fake lottery or prize message, an advance-fee fraud, a fake mobile-money message or phishing e-mail.

questions.enonce_markdown: State THREE components and describe how each can influence the processing power of a computer. (3 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
Any three of the following (one mark each):

1. **Processor (CPU).** Its **clock speed** (GHz), its **number of cores** and the size of its **cache** determine how many instructions are executed per second. A faster processor with more cores and more cache processes data and runs several programs more quickly.
2. **RAM (main memory).** The more RAM there is, the more programs and data can be kept in memory at the same time. With too little RAM the system must swap data with the slow disk (virtual memory), which slows the computer down.
3. **Storage device.** A solid-state drive (SSD) reads and writes data much faster than a hard disk, so programs load faster and virtual memory is less of a bottleneck.

(Other accepted components: the graphics card (GPU), which takes over the graphics work of the CPU, and the width and speed of the bus on the motherboard.)
